channels.name: SoundWire_Clock
channels.direction_master: output (Push-Pull); the single Master drives the Clock continuously while the bus is active.
channels.direction_slave: input only — Slaves never drive SoundWire_Clock; there is no Slave clock-stretching.
channels.purpose: Provides the bus Clock used by all Slaves and optional Monitor. Maximum 13 MHz typical (can be faster in restricted geometries); audio-friendly natural frequencies are 9.6 MHz, 12 MHz, 12.288 MHz. Clock can be paused via ClockStop (Mode 0 mandatory, Mode 1 optional).
channels.active_levels: Push-Pull 0/1 normally; held Low (parked) during ClockStop.
channels.idle_level: Static Low during ClockStop; otherwise active square-wave at programmed natural-clock frequency.

channels.name: SoundWire_Data (Lane 0)
channels.direction_master: bidirectional — Master drives Control Word in Column 0 Rows 0..47 and pulses for assigned Source-port BitSlots; Modified-NRZI encoded.
channels.direction_slave: bidirectional — Slaves drive their per-Slave status bits, Read Data responses, audio payload for assigned Source-port BitSlots, and PREQ.
channels.purpose: Carries the embedded 48-bit Control Word + audio Payload (PCM, PDM, raw DATA, BRA blocks) + PHY arbitration. Modified-NRZI: Logic 1 = active level change, Logic 0 = passive unchanged level held by bus-keeper. DDR — two BitSlots per Clock period.
channels.active_levels: Push-Pull when actively driven; otherwise bus-keeper-held last level.
channels.idle_level: Whatever the bus-keeper last latched; explicitly Low during the Stopping Frame and ClockStop park.

channels.name: SoundWire_Data Lane 1..7 (optional)
channels.direction_master: bidirectional — used when extra payload bandwidth is needed; routed per Port via dynamic switch.
channels.direction_slave: bidirectional — Slave may drive its assigned Source-port BitSlots on any allocated lane.
channels.purpose: Optional additional Data lanes for higher aggregate bandwidth. Lane 0 is shared between all devices (Col 0 Rows 0..47 reserved for Command Word). Lanes 1..7 may be shared or private to a group of devices; for device-to-device lanes a bus-keeper must be enabled on one of the devices. No restrictions on Lane 1..7 — all bits including Col 0 can be used.

global_signals.name: VDD
global_signals.purpose: Supply voltage (1.2 V or 1.8 V typical) for SoundWire I/O drivers.

global_signals.name: GND
global_signals.purpose: Common ground reference for all devices on the bus.

global_signals.name: Bus-Keeper
global_signals.purpose: Required active circuit (typically on Master) that weakly holds the last driven level on SoundWire_Data; can be disabled via M_KeeperOff PHY Test Mode for replacement by external test equipment.

handshake_pairs.name: ADDR_PING_STATUS
handshake_pairs.rule: Slave drives its three-state status (Not Attached / Attached / Alert) at its assigned Device Number position in every PING frame.

handshake_pairs.name: READ_RESPONSE
handshake_pairs.rule: In the Frame after a READ command, addressed Slave drives the 8-bit Read Data payload + Command Status ACK; on parity error → NAK; on non-existent / not-attached / reserved register → Command_Ignored.

handshake_pairs.name: WRITE_RESPONSE
handshake_pairs.rule: In the Frame after a WRITE command, addressed Slave drives Command Status ACK / NAK / Command_Ignored.

handshake_pairs.name: ASYNC_READY_BITS
handshake_pairs.rule: Each sample carries 2-bit preamble (RX-Ready from Sink, TX-Ready from Source); data only transmitted when both Ready.

handshake_pairs.name: BREQ_BREL
handshake_pairs.rule: Monitor Command Word ownership arbitration; BREQ=0 = Master owns; BREQ=1, BREL=1 = Monitor owns; BREQ=0, BREL=1 = illegal.

handshake_pairs.name: WAKE_HIGH
handshake_pairs.rule: Wake-Up High on SoundWire_Data for ≥ 2× minimum BitSlot duration during ClockStop park; Master resumes Clock thereafter.

dependency_graph.common_rule: Master drives SoundWire_Clock continuously (except ClockStop); Slaves sample SoundWire_Data on both Clock edges; all devices observe the 8+1-bit Static + 4-bit Dynamic CRC sync to lock Frame boundaries.
dependency_graph.data_dependency: PING/READ/WRITE in Control Word → addressed Slave decodes during same Frame → Slave responds in next Frame's Command Status / Read Data payload field (1-frame round-trip for READ).
dependency_graph.no_slave_clock_drive: Slaves cannot delay the bus via SoundWire_Clock; the only sequencing tools are the CP_SM / CSP_SM Prepare/Activate state machines, Channel Activation gating, and Bank Switch synchronized to the next SSP tick.

ordering_rules.bit_ordering_in_frame: Bits are transmitted serially in a column-major-within-row bitstream traversing the 2-D Frame (each row's columns are traversed in order, then advance to next row).
ordering_rules.control_word_position: Always the first 48 rows of Column 0 of every Frame.
ordering_rules.ddr_rule: Two BitSlots per Clock period (rising + falling edge).
ordering_rules.block_per_port_ordering: All channels of a port packed lowest-to-highest channel as a single data chunk per Sample Interval.
ordering_rules.block_per_channel_ordering: Each channel in an individual chunk with Block_Offset + Sub_Block_Offset; allows 'holes' in bit allocation reclaimable by other streams (e.g. 48 kHz stereo same pattern as 96 kHz mono).

channel_protocol_layering.phy_layer: Modified-NRZI DDR with bus-keeper; tDZ_Data_Max < tZD_Data_Min; tOH_Data_Min ensures bus-keeper snaps to new value; PHY test modes (M_DataOff / M_ClockDataOff / M_AllOff / M_KeeperOff / M_LowLow / M_LowHigh) supported by Master.
channel_protocol_layering.frame_layer: Configurable 2-D NumCols × NumRows Frame; first 48 rows of Col 0 = Control Word; remaining BitSlots carry payload partitioned into per-Port Transport Sub-Frames.
channel_protocol_layering.transport_layer: Per-Port HStart, HStop, SampleInterval, BlockOffset, SubBlockOffset; Block-Per-Port vs Block-Per-Channel; Isochronous vs Asynchronous (RX-Ready/TX-Ready handshake); per-Port Transport Test Modes Static0/Static1/PRBS mandatory.
channel_protocol_layering.command_layer: Embedded in Control Word — PING, READ (16-bit addr, 8-bit payload), WRITE (16-bit addr, 8-bit payload), BRA on DP0 (~20 Mbit/s).
channel_protocol_layering.management_layer: Enumeration via 48-bit SCP_Device0..5 + hardware arbitration at Device 0; banked SCP_FrameCtrl0/1 for synchronized reconfiguration; ClockStop / ClockStopPrepare; Channel Prepare; Monitor BREQ/BREL arbitration.
